name: The Cinder Vent
_plan: A lava tube the flow emptied out of and left behind, and the one place on Route 5 that is worth going into rather than past. Two galleries with the live flow still running between them: the near one is free, the far one costs a walk over two stepping stones of crust, and everything good is on the far side. The left-hand branch at the bottom -- the one the sign on the road warns about -- is a scald pool with somebody's boots still beside it.

text: Names, scratched into the glaze of the wall. Dozens of them, going back a long way.
ROSE. HALLAM. TEB AND SPARROW. Under all of it, cut much deeper and much older,
a spiral, and a line of marks that are not letters in any hand anyone here writes.
A pair of boots, set neatly side by side at the edge of the water. Nobody in them.
They have been here long enough to go hard. Somebody came out of the pool barefoot,
or somebody did not come out.
The flow is a hand's width below the lip of its own channel and it has been for years.
It is not falling. Whatever is feeding it has not once run short.
